items.title: I’ve been married for 58 years. It’s ‘our’ money, not ‘his’ and ‘hers.’ Why do so many couples keep their finances separate?
items.content: “My wife stopped working outside the home in 1970.”

items.title: My husband secretly sends his ex-wife $1,500 a month after she lost her job. We have $2.4 million saved. Has he lied by omission?
items.content: “He explained that he wasn’t trying to hide the payment, but his former wife lost her job in a medical billing company.”

items.title: My friends play ‘credit-card roulette’ to see who pays for dinner — but one ‘winner’ still Venmoed me afterward. Should I say something?
items.content: ‘I was stunned! I’ve lost my fair share, and won my fair share, and truly believe it all evens out over time.’

items.title: Artificial intelligence usage is exploding, yet spending is stalling. Why a foundational rule of economics is breaking.
items.content: For frontier model lab developers, the increased consumption of AI tokens (the means by which they get paid for their compute) is a positive. However, they don’t seem to be generating revenues from it at the same rate.

items.title: Nvidia’s stock has tumbled 28% over one chaotic month. The next big test lies in the week ahead
items.content: Jensen Huang faces tough questions from Congress this week. Good luck pinning him down, one analyst says.

items.title: How much more are richest Americans spending on the holidays compared to everyone else?
items.content: Most households are getting “squeezed by rising costs of everyday goods,” according to Teneo, but upper-income households “are showing resilience.”

items.title: Clearing out my parents’ house was a legal nightmare. How can I downsize without putting my kids through the same ordeal?
items.content: Some countercultural advice this Black Friday: stop buying stuff, plus other rules for downsizing.

items.title: Renters are now a national political constituency that can influence elections
items.content: Renters backed Democrats 61% to 31% in the midterms, a 30-point margin, according to YouGov.

items.title: New-home sales just hit a 2026 high as builders dangle low mortgages and Black Friday deals
items.content: Sales of newly built homes surged to the highest level of the year in October, as home builders offered aggressive discounts to buyers.
